words: Five platforms kept separate Figma libraries, so tokens diverged and teams repeated component decisions.
Building on React Aria's accessible components let Harmony focus on CASSI's own visual language, content, and interactions.
One shared library became the common reference, with shared governance and defined exceptions.
New projects start on Harmony; existing products migrate gradually, so full adoption is still in progress.
Harmony is now the foundation for new projects at CASSI.
extra:
I lead design and the ongoing evolution of components; the development team implements the React library in partnership with me.

React Aria accelerated component delivery significantly, especially for accessibility criteria. Building fully accessible components from scratch is unrealistic for most teams. By leveraging a battle-tested library, we eliminated solved problems from Harmony's roadmap and focused energy on decisions specific to CASSI: visual language, content standards, and interaction patterns.
